reason: GitHub's own language colors, which kit/github's REST fetcher attaches to each repository's language at render time (#10 moves them into snapshots). They describe the repository, not the site's palette.

Each platform's own brand colors, for a link card that shows the platform's identity rather than the site's, plus a default and an email entry in the retired v1 palette; nothing imports the module, and it retires with them.

The 40px and 60px blurs are the aurora itself: two colored gradients blurred until they read as light. No design language's backdrop blur, which frosts what's behind a surface, draws that, and the colors are the boundary's.
The panel's edge glow, a halo in the boundary's accent, is the effect: no design language's shadow draws a colored glow, and its color is the boundary's accent unless the caller gives one.
The cursor's halo and dot are circles, which a 50% radius draws in every design language; a design language's radius sets a surface's corners, not a circle's shape.
A known-bad budget fixture (#6) that only BUDGET_FIXTURES=over registers: its remote @import and its ballast sheet are what the budget check has to report, so the audit has to let them stand here.

The same known-bad budget fixture's ballast, generated by packages/budget-fixtures/ballast.mjs: custom properties holding bytes nothing can compress, there only to keep the fixture over its CSS budget, which only BUDGET_FIXTURES=over registers.

A budget fixture (#6) that only BUDGET_FIXTURES=1 registers, whose infinite 2.4 s pulse is the CSS animation the medium tier's budget counts. It never ships, and the pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

The preview's environment fixture (#7), which only PREVIEW_FIXTURES=1 registers: its 1.2 s pulse is the animation the preview tests read by name, running in a full environment and gone in a reduced one, so it has to run on its own.

The same fixture is styled by the environment attributes alone, with no pack, so the preview tests can read what each environment does: it paints in the system colors Canvas and CanvasText, which every display mode and forced colors define.
The same fixture's --fe-rule, the rule width each environment sets and the preview tests read back, since the fixture has no design language to read one from.
The same fixture renders with no typography pack, so its text takes the system font, system-ui, behind a property of its own nothing sets; nothing ships it.
